reports.title: 2026 Property Tax and Supplementary Property Tax Bylaw (Bylaw 21442)
reports.description: Annual bylaw under section 353 of the Municipal Government Act authorizing municipal, education and Designated Industrial Property requisition tax rates against the assessment roll and provincial assessment roll for the taxation year. Passed 28 April 2026; sets residential municipal rate at 0.0077419 and non-residential at 0.0252216 among other classes.

reports.title: City of Edmonton Approved Operating Budget (multi-year cycle with annual tax-levy confirmation)
reports.description: Detailed tax-supported and utility operating budget for the current year within the 2023-2026 multi-year framework, finalized via spring tax-levy confirmation. 2026 version incorporates a 6.9% municipal tax increase and funds core services, debt servicing and transfers.

reports.title: City of Edmonton Annual Report — Consolidated Audited Financial Statements
reports.description: Annual consolidated audited financial statements (Statement of Financial Position, Operations, Cash Flows and notes) prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards for the year ended 31 December, including tax-supported operations, utilities, EPCOR equity accounting and education tax remittances. 2025 edition released spring 2026.

reports.title: Property Assessment Notices / Assessment Roll
reports.description: Annual market-value assessment notices mailed to property owners (January) under the Municipal Government Act, forming the assessment roll against which tax rates are levied. Values reflect the prior-year July 1 market condition; open data extract of assessed values also published.

reports.title: Saskatchewan Budget — Fiscal Plan / Summary Financial Statements Outlook
reports.description: Annual provincial budget documents (Budget Address, Estimates, Highlights, Fiscal Outlook) setting revenue, expense and deficit projections for the fiscal year beginning 1 April. 2026-27 edition projects $21.4 billion revenue, $22.2 billion expense and an $819 million deficit, with multi-year outlook to surplus in 2030-31.

reports.title: Saskatchewan Assessment Management Agency (SAMA) — Assessment Governance, Valuation Services and Roll Confirmation
reports.description: Provincial agency responsible for property assessment policy, valuation services to ~760 municipalities, quality assurance audits, and statutory confirmation of municipal assessment rolls. Publishes annual report, revaluation manuals (four-year cycle), business plan and confirmed assessment totals; assessment base ~$278 billion supporting ~$2.6 billion in property taxes.

reports.title: SAMA Annual Report
reports.description: Annual report of SAMA operations, financial results, property review volumes, confirmed assessment totals by class and municipal type, and quality-assurance audit outcomes for the preceding calendar year.

reports.title: Manitoba Budget — Summary Budget and Financial Updates
reports.description: Annual Summary Budget prepared under GAAP presenting consolidated revenue, expense, operating surplus/deficit and net debt for the fiscal year ending 31 March. 2026/27 edition projects $26.8 billion revenue, $27.3 billion expense and a $498 million deficit, with medium-term path to small surpluses.

reports.title: Manitoba Property Assessment Services (Municipal and Northern Relations)
reports.publisher: Manitoba Municipal and Northern Relations — Property Assessment Services
reports.description: Provincial assessment authority responsible for market-value assessment of all real and personal property outside the City of Winnipeg (approximately 440 000 roll entries). Conducts regular reassessments, maintains Manitoba Assessment Online, and recovers costs via the statutory Property Assessment Levy on municipalities. Winnipeg maintains its own assessment function.
reports.cadence_note: continuous (reassessment cycle typically biennial or as legislated)

reports.title: City of Winnipeg Multi-Year Budget — 2026 Update (Operating, Reserves and Capital)
reports.description: Annual update to the 2024-2027 multi-year operating, reserves and capital budget. 2026 edition sets a 3.5% municipal property tax increase (mill rate 13.372) dedicated partly to roads and tax-supported operations; total City revenue approximately $2.5 billion.

reports.title: City of Winnipeg Annual Financial Report — Consolidated Audited Financial Statements
reports.description: Annual consolidated audited financial statements prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards for the year ended 31 December, covering tax-supported operations, utilities and controlled entities. 2025 edition available; 2024 edition also published.

reports.title: City of Winnipeg Property Assessment Roll / Notices
reports.publisher: City of Winnipeg Assessment and Taxation Department
reports.description: Annual (and general reassessment-cycle) market-value assessment of properties within Winnipeg. Portioned at class-specific percentages (residential 45%). 2027 general assessment roll delivery announced for June 2026; City maintains its own assessment function separate from provincial Property Assessment Services.

reports.title: The Saskatoon Property Tax Bylaw, 2026 (Bylaw No. 10174)
reports.description: Annual bylaw under The Cities Act authorizing municipal and library mill rates and mill-rate factors against taxable assessments for 2026. Uniform municipal rate 9.1147 mills; residential tax rate 0.0080291 after factors. Passed 29 April 2026.

reports.title: City of Saskatoon Multi-Year Business Plan and Budget (Operating, Capital & Climate)
reports.description: Multi-year operating, capital and climate budget approved by Council. 2026/2027 edition incorporates tax-supported revenue share of approximately 51% and rate increases for utilities; taxation remains the largest single revenue source.

reports.title: City of Saskatoon Annual Report — Consolidated Financial Statements
reports.description: Annual consolidated financial statements and statistical section prepared under Canadian public sector accounting standards. 2024 edition reports taxation revenue of $347.8 million and total consolidated operating revenues of $1.31 billion.

reports.title: City of Saskatoon Property Assessment Roll / Notices
reports.description: Annual assessment notices and public assessment roll prepared under provincial legislation with SAMA oversight. 2025 was a provincially legislated revaluation year (base date 2023); next full revaluation 2029. Supplemental assessments issued for physical changes.

reports.title: SAMA Municipal Assessment Return (annual form and confirmation process)
reports.description: Standardised annual return submitted by municipalities to SAMA Quality Assurance for confirmation of the assessment roll. Required under The Assessment Management Agency Act; once confirmed, the roll is valid for tax enforcement. Blank form, checklist and sample published each year; Certificates of Confirmation issued and gazetted.

reports.title: City of Regina Annual Budget (Operating and Capital)
reports.description: Annual operating and capital budget adopted under The Cities Act. 2026 edition approved December 2025 with a 10.9% mill-rate increase; focuses on core services, police, fire and infrastructure renewal.

reports.title: The Regina Property Tax Bylaw (annual)
reports.description: Annual bylaw establishing municipal, library and school mill rates and mill-rate factors against taxable assessments. 2025 edition (Bylaw 2025-30) available; 2026 rates published on City tax-calculation pages (municipal mill rate factors applied to base rates).

reports.title: The Regina Property Tax Bylaw, 2026 (Bylaw No. 2026-25)
reports.description: Annual bylaw under The Cities Act establishing municipal, library and business-improvement-district tax rates against taxable assessments sufficient to meet the 2026 budgets of the City and Library. Companion Education Property Tax Bylaw 2026-24 and Property Classes Bylaw 2026-23 also enacted.

reports.title: City of Regina Annual Report — Consolidated Audited Financial Statements
reports.description: Annual consolidated audited financial statements and Public Accounts required under The Cities Act ss. 155-156. 2025 edition (year ended 31 December 2025) approved by Audit and Finance Committee May 2026 and recommended to Council; 2024 Public Accounts and Annual Report previously published on open data.

reports.title: Manitoba Municipal Financial Plan and Tax Levy By-law Filing
reports.description: Statutory annual process under The Municipal Act requiring every municipality to adopt and file a Financial Plan (by 15 May) and a Tax Levy By-law (by 15 June) with the Province, followed by audited financial statements. Provides the provincial oversight layer for municipal budgets and tax rates outside Winnipeg; no centralized compiled FIR-style dataset is published.

dependencies.basis: Bylaw 21442 is enacted pursuant to MGA s. 353 to raise the revenue required to meet the expenditures and transfers set out in the municipality’s budget. The document states: "pursuant to section 353 of the Municipal Government Act ... City Council must pass a property tax bylaw annually authorizing the Council to impose a tax in respect of property in the municipality to raise revenue to be used toward the payment of the expenditures and transfers set out in the budget of the municipality, and the requisitions"

The bylaw authorizes the CAO to levy the rates against the assessed value of all taxable property shown on the Assessment Roll and the Provincial Assessment Roll. The document states: "The Chief Administrative Officer is hereby authorized to levy the tax rate set out in Schedule "A" against the assessed value of all taxable property ... shown on the Assessment Roll and the Supplementary Assessment Roll"

The bylaw levies education tax rates to satisfy the Alberta School Foundation Fund and Edmonton Catholic Separate School District requisitions. The document states: "The City is required to levy a tax to pay the requisition from the Province for the Alberta School Foundation Fund under section 167 of the Education Act ... and the requisition by the Edmonton Catholic Separate School District No. 7"

The bylaw authorizes levy of the Designated Industrial Property Requisition at the rate set by Ministerial Order against the Provincial Assessment Roll for DIP properties. The document states: "The property tax rate for the 2026 Designated Industrial Property (DIP) Requisition by the Province of Alberta is 0.0000728 (Ministerial Order No.: MAG:003/26)"
dependencies.evidence_quote: The property tax rate for the 2026 Designated Industrial Property (DIP) Requisition by the Province of Alberta is 0.0000728 (Ministerial Order No.: MAG:003/26)

dependencies.basis: The consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards as established by the Public Sector Accounting Board. The document states: "the City’s consolidated financial statements and notes, which have been prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards (PSAS)"
dependencies.evidence_quote: the City’s consolidated financial statements and notes, which have been prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards (PSAS)

dependencies.basis: Operating budget information for the year is stated to be consistent with the amounts approved by Council via the Property Tax Bylaw; budget columns appear beside actuals. The document states: "Operating budget information for 2025 is consistent with the amounts approved by City Council (Council) in April 2025 with the passing of Bylaw 21068 - 2025 Property Tax and Supplementary Property Tax Bylaw"

Federal transfers, including equalization, form a material revenue line in the provincial fiscal outlook and are explicitly referenced in budget materials as contributing to revenue growth. The document states: "Increased revenue is driven primarily by gains in provincial sales tax (PST) and federal transfers reflecting Saskatchewan’s growing population and strong economic conditions"

The annual report is the statutory and operational reporting vehicle of the Agency itself. The document states: "SAMA is responsible for assessment governance of the estimated $278 Billion property assessment base, and a $2.64 Billion property tax base"

Federal transfers, including equalization, are a major revenue source explicitly quantified in the Summary Budget. The document states: "$727M or 8.1% increase in federal transfers reflecting increases in equalization, CHT, CST and other federal transfers"
The Canada Health Transfer is named among the federal transfers driving the revenue increase in Budget 2026. The document states: "increases in equalization, CHT, CST and other federal transfers"

Assessment services costs are recovered in part through the provincial budget process and the statutory levy; the department reports within the broader provincial fiscal framework. The document states: "Assessment Services is responsible for the assessment of all real and personal property in the province, excluding property in the City of Winnipeg"

Consolidated financial statements are prepared in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards. The document states: "These consolidated financial statements have been audited by KPMG LLP ... in accordance with Canadian public sector accounting standards."

Financial statements report budget-to-actual comparisons for tax-supported operations and reference the multi-year budget process. The document states: "The 2025 Budget Update builds on the work done in 2024. It focuses on Winnipeggers' top priorities: safer neighbourhoods, and better roads."

The bylaw authorizes the uniform rate considered sufficient to raise the amount of taxes required to meet the estimated expenditures and transfers set out in the budget of the City for 2026. The document states: "authorize Council to impose a tax on all taxable assessments in the City at a uniform rate considered sufficient to raise the amount of taxes required to meet the estimated expenditures and transfers, having regard to estimated revenues from other sources, set out in the budget of the City for 2026"

Tax rates and mill-rate factors are applied to taxable assessments shown on the assessment roll. The document states: "Council is authorized to impose a tax on all taxable assessments in the City at the following rates for 2026"

Assessments are prepared under provincial legislation with oversight from SAMA; percentages of value and property classes are set provincially. The document states: "The City of Saskatoon determines assessments based on legislation and direction from the provincial agency that provides assessment oversight, the Saskatchewan Assessment Management Agency (SAMA)."
dependencies.evidence_quote: The City of Saskatoon determines assessments based on legislation and direction from the provincial agency that provides assessment oversight, the Saskatchewan Assessment Management Agency (SAMA).

dependencies.basis: Budget-to-actual comparisons appear throughout the financial highlights and statistical sections. The document states: "BUDGET TO ACTUAL AND PRIOR YEAR COMPARISON"

The bylaw establishes tax rates sufficient to meet the estimated expenditures and transfers set out in the budgets of the City and the Library. The document states: "establish tax rates and impose taxes on ... all taxable property in the City of Regina sufficient to meet the estimated expenditures and transfers ... set out in the budgets of the City and the Library"

dependencies.basis: Property assessments and percentages of value follow provincial rules administered with SAMA oversight. The document states: "The provincial percentage is a factor set by the Province of Saskatchewan to adjust the assessment used as the basis for calculating property tax."

The bylaw’s purpose is to establish tax rates sufficient to meet the estimated expenditures and transfers set out in the budgets of the City and the Library for 2026. The document states: "establish tax rates and impose taxes on: (a) all taxable property in the City of Regina sufficient to meet the estimated expenditures and transfers, having regard to estimated revenues from other sources, set out in the budgets of the City and the Library for 2026"
